label: Milton William Cooper
narrative: Milton William Cooper is a propagation node and the board should be precise about what he propagated, because the usual account overstates it. His paper 'The Secret Government', dated on its own first page 23 May 1989 and updated 21 November 1990, delivered at the MUFON symposium in Las Vegas on 2 July 1989 and later absorbed into his 1991 book Behold a Pale Horse, was extracted and searched in full for this cluster. It contains the frame: 'It was agreed that bases would be constructed underground for the use of the alien nation and that two bases would be constructed for the joint use of the alien nation and the United States Government...These alien bases would be constructed under Indian reservations in the Four Corners area of Utah, Colorado, New Mexico and Arizona, and one would be constructed in an area known as Dreamland.' IT DOES NOT CONTAIN THE WORD DULCE. The string occurs zero times in forty-nine pages. A count is checkable and an adjective is not, which is why the number is carried in the claim rather than a characterisation. Cooper's edge to the hub is therefore Tier 3 frame-propagation and nothing stronger. Two further things belong on the node. First, he graded his own document: after describing his sources as top secret material seen between 1970 and 1973 as a member of the Intelligence Briefing Team of the Commander in Chief of the Pacific Fleet, plus sources he could not divulge and 'published sources which I cannot vouch for', he writes that 'this chapter must be termed a hypothesis'. The board should use the author's own grade. Second, the same document independently corroborates one element of the Kirtland affair: Cooper writes that Linda Moulton Howe 'confided to me that Sgt. Richard Doty of the Counterintelligence Division of the Air Force Office of Special Investigations had taken her into the Intelligence office at Kirtland Air Force Base in New Mexico and showed her the exact same documents that I had seen'. That corroborates that Howe was telling the story by 1989 to a third party. It corroborates nothing about the documents themselves.
